**Chapter 9: Acid-Base Balance**

**9.1 Reaction between dilute NaOH and Fe(NO3)3**

If we take some ferric nitrate Fe(NO3)3 solution in a test tube and add some drops of dilute NaOH solution in it, they produce ferric hydroxide [Fe(OH)3] and sodium nitrate (NaNO3). Fe(OH)3 gathers as a reddish brown precipitate at the bottom of the test tube while sodium nitrate remains dissolved in the water and it does not add any color to the water. The reaction:

Fe(NO3)3 + 3NaOH → Fe(OH)3 + 3NaNO3

**9.2 Reaction between dilute NaOH and Cu(NO3)2**

If we take some copper nitrate [Cu(NO3)2] solution in a test tube and add some drops of dilute NaOH solution to it, copper hydroxide [Cu(OH)2] and sodium nitrate (NaNO3) are produced. Cu(OH)2 gathers as light blue precipitate at the bottom of the test tube while sodium nitrate remains dissolved in the water and it does not add any color to the water. The reaction:

Cu(NO3)2 + 2NaOH → Cu(OH)2 + 2NaNO3

**9.3 Reaction between dilute NaOH and Zn(NO3)2**

If we take some zinc nitrate [Zn(NO3)2] solution in a test tube and add some drops of dilute NaOH solution to it, zinc hydroxide [Zn(OH)2] and sodium nitrate (NaNO3) are produced. Fe(OH)2 gathers as white precipitate at the bottom of the test tube while sodium nitrate remains dissolved in the water and it does not add any color to the water. The reaction:

Zn(NO3)2 + 2NaOH → Zn(OH)2 + 2NaNO3

**9.4 Reaction between Alkali (dilute NaOH) and Ammonium Salt**

If we take some ammonium chloride (NH4Cl) in a container and add some alkali (NaOH) solution to it, we get ammonia gas (NH3), sodium chloride (NaCl) and water (H2O). The reaction:

NH4Cl + NaOH → NH3 + NaCl + H2O
